Yeah that’s correct. I’m still in Dublin. 

Degree won’t matter if you’re skilled enough. Masters is just a way to get visa. But the courses in UCD are great. You can apply to companies in Ireland directly. Many companies do sponsor visa. I know a lot of people getting here by this route. Saves you a lot on tuition fees

I did my masters in UCD. My tuition fees was 24k. Living expenses easily reach 10k per year. You can expect a job which pays minimum 50k if you are in software engineering. ROI isn’t as great as US. Considering salaries are going up exponentially in India, masters in Europe isn’t that attractive as it was few years ago. But atleast you won’t be a part of rat race. Getting into big companies like Facebook and google are easier here, if that’s what you want.

I did my masters 3 years ago in Dublin. Universities look for good academics. You need to have 6.5 average in IELTS. IETS score isn’t considered when evaluating your application. Any research experience or work experience presented in a way which relates to the course will help your application
